findings.label: Giant coronary artery aneurysm
findings.evidence: Caption identifies a “giant” coronary aneurysm affecting the mid segment of the right coronary artery in a patient with history of Kawasaki disease.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is a coronary angiogram of a 19-year-old patient with Kawasaki disease and visibly demonstrates the captioned giant right coronary artery aneurysm. B: Panel B is a 3D reconstructed CT image from the same 19-year-old patient with prior Kawasaki disease, demonstrating the captioned giant coronary aneurysm.

panels.figure_caption: Giant coronary artery aneurysm. (A) Coronary angiogram of a 19 year-old male patient with history of Kawasaki disease during childhood showing a “giant” coronary aneurysm affecting the mid segment of the right coronary artery. (B) 3D volume-rendered reconstructed CT image of the same patient.
in_text_mentions: arteries – including aneurysmal and stenotic lesions – may have already occurred. The sizes of coronary aneurysms are classified as small (<5 mm internal diameter), medium (5-8 mm) and giant (>8 mm) (Figure 2).32 Regression of small and medium sized aneurysms to normal lumen diameter occurs in approximately half the cases within 2 years from the onset of illness. In contrast, obstructive lesions develop in 2 years and continue to increase over time.36 Stenotic lesions occur as a result of luminal myofibroblastic proliferation and thrombosis. in_text_mentions: A diagnosis of atypical Kawasaki was considered and echocardiography was requested. The day after admission, he had desquamation of the skin at his fingertips and perianal region (Figure 2). Echocardiographic examination revealed saccular dilatation of the origin of left main coronary artery (LCA) and aneurysmal dilatation of left anterior descending (LAD) artery (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph from a child case series of Kawasaki disease. The caption and image directly support periungual desquamation, a characteristic mucocutaneous manifestation of Kawasaki disease. No coronary imaging or other panel is present in this figure.
